title: Joint Statement on the Launch of Trilateral Technical Planning Groups to Advance the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP)
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 6, 2026
The following text was released by the Governments of the United States of America, Armenia, and Azerbaijan.
Begin Text.
Today, U.S. Assistant Secretary of State for European and Eurasian Affairs Brendan Hanrahan, Armenian Deputy Foreign Minister Vahan Kostanyan, and Azerbaijani Deputy Foreign Minister Elnur Mammadov launched Trilateral Technical Planning Groups to advance the Trump Route for International Peace and Prosperity (TRIPP), a multimodal transit route. This forum brings together policymakers and technical experts from our three countries to work collaboratively and contribute to long-term stability, economic vitality, regional connectivity, and commercial prosperity across the region, underscoring the landmark August 8, 2025, Peace Summit Declaration brokered by President Trump.
Demonstrating a shared commitment to turn vision into tangible progress, the parties agreed to inaugurate the first two Trilateral Planning Groups focused on transportation and electricity transmission. These technical planning groups represent a crucial step toward resolving complex technical issues and moving to the next phases of implementation, including connection with other regional infrastructures.
The sides reaffirmed their respective commitments to expeditious operationalization of all modalities of TRIPP.
End Text.

title: U.S. Sanctions Cripple Financial Networks Sustaining the Iranian Regime
summary_raw:
Thomas "Tommy" Pigott, SpokesmanOffice of the Spokesman
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
November 6, 2026
The United States is taking action today against eight digital asset service providers that help the Iranian regime evade sanctions and fund terrorism. The Department of the Treasury is designating these firms, which exchange Iranian rials and other currencies for digital assets so that the regime, the Islamic Revolutionary Guard Corps (IRGC), and other sanctioned actors can move money into and out of Iran.
Several of these businesses sent funds to digital asset accounts linked to the IRGC and other terrorist activity. Many also dealt with Iranian cryptocurrency exchanges that the United States has already sanctioned. Some changed their names and addresses to avoid detection, and all of them kept operating despite public reporting on the risks they posed.
As part of Operation Economic Outcast, the United States will continue to cut off revenue the Iranian regime uses to fund terrorism, weapons proliferation, and its proxies across the Middle East. Today’s action deepens Iran’s economic isolation and targets its growing use of digital assets to get around sanctions. It follows U.S. sanctions earlier this year on Iranian digital asset exchanges that moved money for the regime and the IRGC. Anyone, anywhere in the world, who helps Tehran evade sanctions risks being held accountable.
The United States coordinated this action closely with Canada, including Canada’s financial intelligence unit, FINTRAC. It reflects our shared commitment to protecting the North American financial system from abuse. Several of the designated businesses also laundered proceeds from drug trafficking, which shows how the same illicit networks serve both Iran and criminal organizations that threaten the safety of our communities. We will keep working with Canada and other international partners to expose these networks, shut them down, and make sure no country becomes a refuge for people who finance terrorism and evade sanctions.
Today’s designations are imposed pursuant to Executive Order (E.O.) 13902, which targets the Iranian digital asset sector, among other key sectors of the Iranian economy. For more information, please see Treasury’s press release.

title: U.S. Department of State Announces Selection for the 2027 Venice Architecture Biennale
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 6, 2026

Today, the Department of State announced the selection of The University of Miami School of Architecture to represent the United States at the 20th Venice Architecture Biennale.  The 2027 U.S. Pavilion exhibition, Earth Craft, is organized by Lead Curator Germane Barnes, Associate Professor and Director of the Master of Architecture Graduate Program at the University of Miami School of Architecture and Principal of Studio Barnes.  The exhibition will look at how American architecture is shaped by the land and the people who build on it.  It will follow earthen materials, including brick, rammed earth, adobe, and concrete masonry, from the ground to the finished building.  It will also recognize the brickmakers, masons, and builders who used American soil to build the homes, schools, and public buildings found across the United States.  The Bureau of Educational and Cultural Affairs supports and manages the official U.S. participation at Venice Arts and Architecture Biennales to showcase the excellence of American art and culture on the world stage.
For additional information, please contact eca-press@state.gov.

title: Joint Statement on the Second Meeting of the Joint Steering Committee of the U.S.-DRC Strategic Partnership Agreement
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 6, 2026
The text of the following statement was released by the Governments of the United States of America and the Democratic Republic of the Congo.
Begin text.
Representatives from the Government of the United States and the Government of the Democratic Republic of the Congo (DRC) met in Paris for the second meeting of the Joint Steering Committee (JSC) of the U.S.-DRC Strategic Partnership Agreement. Representatives from both governments reaffirmed their shared commitment to economic growth, stability, and prosperity for both our peoples.
The JSC provides strategic direction for implementing the Agreement and helps turn its commitments into concrete initiatives with clear responsibilities, realistic timelines, and measurable outcomes. JSC members emphasized the importance of close coordination among the relevant ministries, agencies, and technical institutions of both governments, supported by regular monitoring and follow-up.
The JSC reviewed progress since the inaugural meeting in February 2026 and welcomed growing U.S. private sector interest in the Strategic Asset Reserve (SAR). The U.S. International Development Finance Corporation (DFC) briefed on its growing investment pipeline in the DRC.
The JSC recognized important milestones on the DRC Designated Strategic Projects, including the signing of the concession agreement for the Lobito Corridor, a key step toward stronger regional trade and connectivity. The delegations also discussed next steps on the Grand Inga hydropower project and explored critical minerals processing, export, and energy sector opportunities for U.S. companies.
JSC members noted the DRC’s recent adoption of legislation that sets the tax and customs rules for projects under the Strategic Partnership Agreement and committed to continued close coordination on its implementation. The JSC emphasized the goal of ensuring Congolese citizens and workers benefit from the country’s wealth through job creation, skills development, and the growth of Congolese and American companies. The JSC underscored that clear and timely implementation of related policies will help attract and sustain transparent, long-term investment in the DRC.
The delegations reaffirmed that peace and security are fundamental to the objectives of the Strategic Partnership Agreement and remain the foundation for lasting prosperity in the DRC.
The JSC recognizes the vital role of the private sector in driving economic progress and building stronger commercial ties between the two countries, and encourages eligible companies to take advantage of the opportunities the Strategic Partnership Agreement creates. Interested companies may contact either government as implementation moves forward.
Both governments look forward to turning the Strategic Partnership Agreement’s commitments into lasting investment that creates jobs, strengthens supply chains, and brings shared prosperity to the American and Congolese peoples.
End text.

title: Congratulating Grenada’s Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell on his Reelection
summary_raw:
Marco Rubio, Secretary of State
Press Statement


			
			


			
			
November 6, 2026

The United States congratulates Prime Minister Dickon Mitchell on his electoral victory.  We look forward to continuing our strong collaboration with the Government of Grenada on our shared priorities, including energy development, growing our transparent and reliable trade and investment partnerships, and enhancing regional security and resilience.  Together, we will seek opportunities to support economic growth, energy security, and greater prosperity for both Americans and Grenadians.

title: Joint Statement on the Conviction of Hong Kong Alliance Leaders and Sentencing of Joshua Wong
summary_raw:
Office of the Spokesman
Media Note


			
			


			
			
November 6, 2026

The text of the following statement was released by Governments of the United States of America, Australia, Canada, France, Germany, Italy, Japan, the Netherlands, New Zealand, and the United Kingdom. 
Begin Text.
Joshua Wong was sentenced to 10 years’ imprisonment following a further charge under the National Security Law (NSL).  This comes just months after leaders of the Hong Kong Alliance were convicted under the same legislation. These are further examples of how the NSL is being used to target individuals for political expression and participation.  We call for an immediate end to all unjust prosecutions of individuals charged under the NSL and urge the authorities in China and Hong Kong to uphold their international commitments and honor the rights and freedoms guaranteed to the people of Hong Kong under the Sino-British Joint Declaration (1984).
 End Text.
